body: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1, section "6.1 Areas between Curves", prints these objectives: "Determine the area of a region between two curves by integrating with respect to the independent variable." "Find the area of a compound region." "Determine the area of a region between two curves by integrating with respect to the dependent variable.". The section text says: "In Introduction to Integration , we developed the concept of the definite integral to calculate the area below a curve on a given interval. In this section, we expand that idea to calculate the area of more complex regions. We start by finding the area between two curves that are functions of x , beginning with the simple case in which one function value is always greater than the other. We then look at cases when the graphs of the functions cross. Last, we consider how to calculate the area…" This card reports that page. The objectives are the book's learning statements, not a separate proof.
